sources.title: Hind Swaraj
sources.author: Mohandas K. Gandhi
sources.excerpt: True civilization is that mode of conduct which points out to man the path of duty.
sources.longExcerpt: True civilization is that mode of conduct which points out to man the path of duty. This historical source from 1909 provides valuable insight into the asia region during the industrial period. It represents the voices, experiences, and perspectives of people who lived during this transformative time in human history. Such primary sources are essential for understanding not just the major events of history, but the daily lives, beliefs, and struggles of ordinary people across different cultures and time periods.

sources.title: Asian Industrial Chronicle
sources.author: Various Authors
sources.excerpt: A collection of industrial texts from the Asian region.
sources.longExcerpt: This represents a compilation of historical documents from the Industrial period in the Asian region. These sources provide insight into the daily life, beliefs, and experiences of people during this time. While specific texts vary, they collectively paint a picture of human civilization's development across different cultures and time periods. Such documents are invaluable for understanding how societies evolved and interacted throughout history.

additional_sources.title: Diary of a Silk Factory Girl
additional_sources.author: Yamamoto Masae
additional_sources.excerpt: We rise at 4:30 and work begins at 5:00. The silk threads break often in the humid weather. My fingers are always sore from the boiling water.

additional_sources.title: Letters from Gold Mountain
additional_sources.author: Chen Ming
additional_sources.excerpt: We blast through granite mountains to lay the iron road. Half our wages we save to send home. America is not golden, but the money is real.

additional_sources.title: Accounts of the Bengal Famine
additional_sources.author: Kali Charan Ghosh
additional_sources.excerpt: Rice sells at thirty rupees a maund. People are eating grass and leaves. The children no longer cry; they have no strength left.

additional_sources.title: Diary of Commissioner Lin
additional_sources.author: Lin Zexu
additional_sources.excerpt: The foreign poison has spread through our provinces. Sons steal from fathers to buy opium. I have seized 20,000 chests and dissolved them in the sea.

additional_sources.title: Royal Proclamation on Modernization
additional_sources.author: King Chulalongkorn
additional_sources.excerpt: Slavery shall be gradually abolished. Children born to slaves from this day shall be free. We must adapt or be colonized like our neighbors.

additional_sources.title: Korean Declaration of Independence
additional_sources.author: The Representatives of the Korean People
additional_sources.excerpt: We herewith proclaim the independence of Korea and the liberty of the Korean people. This we proclaim to all nations of the world.
